subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram partial-stream finalization lacks clear delivery-mode observability (sent vs preview-finalized vs canceled)

question: Should Telegram partial-stream finals be fixed as a narrow delivered-state and delivery-outcome repair, or expanded into a new strict fresh-final mode/config surface?
rationale: Current source proves the delivered-state bug, but the issue also asks for outcome taxonomy and an optional strict mode; automation should not choose the permanent Telegram delivery policy or add config surface while an open candidate PR is already linked.

options.title: Narrow Delivered-State Repair
options.body: Rebase or replace the linked PR so delivered state is recorded only after final chunks settle, add explicit outcome signals, and require real Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Add Strict Fresh-Final Mode
options.body: Approve a separate product/config direction that forces fresh final messages for observability and adds migration/docs/tests for that setting.

options.title: Fold Into Cross-Channel Contract
options.body: Defer the Telegram-specific repair into the broader durable delivery contract at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 and keep this issue as a linked proving case.

recommendation.title: Narrow Delivered-State Repair
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace the linked PR so delivered state is recorded only after final chunks settle, add explicit outcome signals, and require real Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Telegram streaming delivery policy and current blamed dispatcher/lane-delivery code where steipete has the strongest recent ownership signal.
